key_insight: C$^2$R adds cross-sample consistency regularization to sparse autoencoders so each semantic feature is more likely to map to one stable latent, reducing feature splitting and absorption.
engineering_relevance: This improves the interpretability of large SAE dictionaries for LLM analysis while preserving reconstruction quality, making latent-feature auditing more reliable at scale.
method: Penalize co-activation of directionally similar latents across samples.
Encourage a unified latent assignment for the same semantic feature within a batch.
Use consistency regularization alongside standard SAE reconstruction/sparsity objectives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comprehensive evaluation showing C$^2$R mitigates splitting and absorption while maintaining reconstruction fidelity.
watch_item: The added cross-sample constraint may require careful tuning to avoid over-regularizing rare or genuinely multi-faceted features.
paper_title: C$^{2}$R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
